# Blueprint

> Blueprint helps a business turn one recurring job into a scoped, funded, measurable robot pilot and decide what happens afterward.

Show Blueprint one recurring job, including phone footage and a proposed pilot price and conditions or a target budget. Keep ongoing economics separate. An approved budget is not required to start. Robot teams evaluate the job for free. No match, no fee. When a robot team passes the evaluation, fits the site's budget, and wants to run the pilot, Blueprint introduces the two sides by name and charges the site $2,500 per job, however many teams match; teams that do not match stay anonymous. The site and the team agree the pilot directly, and Blueprint takes no percentage of the pilot or any deployment. The provider or integrator installs and operates the robot. Simulation is not physical proof or a deployment guarantee.

The site explicitly authorizes the match fee when opening a job to pilot proposals. It is invoiced at introduction even if no pilot is purchased. If a matched team withdraws or materially changes its confirmed price or scope before the pilot starts, Blueprint seeks a replacement that meets the same agreed requirements. If none fits, Blueprint refunds the match fee. Contact hello@tryblueprint.io with the job link.

- [Home](https://tryblueprint.io/)

- [Discuss your site](https://tryblueprint.io/contact/site-operator)
- [Robot teams: apply for early access](https://tryblueprint.io/contact/robot-team)
- [Privacy](https://tryblueprint.io/privacy)
- [Terms](https://tryblueprint.io/terms)

Robot teams join by early access. Approved teams see only job cards sites chose to share. Invited evaluations are free within a bounded scope, carry no supplier commission, and share results with the site for pilot consideration. When a team passes, fits the site's budget, and wants the pilot, Blueprint introduces it to the site, and the two sides agree the pilot directly. The beta offers free invited evaluations only; private paid evaluations and top-ups are unavailable. Pricing: https://tryblueprint.io/pricing. Contact: hello@tryblueprint.io.

## Evidence boundary

Customer wording uses “job” for the work a site wants automated and “task” for the specific robot action and its technical conditions. API fields and identifiers retain their existing names.

A Task Evaluation Run returns a decision or abstention. Pipeline owns method qualification and routing; physical outcomes remain distinct from simulation and generated evidence.

## Agent interfaces and compatibility

Current public/request tools are `blueprint.siteWorld.search`, `blueprint.catalog.search`, `blueprint.ask`, `blueprint.request.locationDraft`, `blueprint.siteWorld.get`, and `blueprint.siteWorld.launchReadiness`.

The historical read and hosted-session compatibility tools are `blueprint.commerce.order.get`, `blueprint.commerce.liveOrder.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlement.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlementReadiness`, `blueprint.session.create`, `blueprint.session.reset`, `blueprint.session.step`, `blueprint.session.runBatch`, `blueprint.session.control`, `blueprint.session.renderExplorer`, and `blueprint.session.export`. Historical availability does not make these current standalone products.

Team account and checkpoint tools use a revocable per-team agent key bound to a verified Blueprint account. Early-access library admission remains required (403 `early_access_required` otherwise). During the free beta, paid planning, dry-run purchase, run-start and top-up APIs return 403 `paid_evaluations_disabled`, including requests with `confirm: true`. Request an invited evaluation through the workspace. Execution requires operator approval of the exact team, policy, task, current rights, expiry, one attempt, and a separate Blueprint-funded compute limit. Historical balances and receipts remain available under their original access controls.

Truth labels are `capture_grounded`, `provider_derived`, `generated`, `request_gated`, `protected_robot_team`, `legacy_commerce_read_only`, and `decision_or_abstention`.
